reason: The text demonstrates God's explicit actions to benefit the Hebrew people: (1) God promises to liberate them from Egyptian slavery; (2) twice states that God grants the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians (וַיִּתֵּן יְהוָה אֶת־ חֵן הָעָם בְּעֵינֵי מִצְרָיִם); (3) the Israelites are specifically protected during the plague—the text explicitly notes that no harm comes to them (וּלְכֹל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יֶֽחֱרַץ־ כֶּלֶב); (4) God facilitates their acquisition of silver, gold, and clothing from the Egyptians; and (5) God orchestrates their departure and freedom. These concrete, divinely-enabled outcomes—liberation from slavery, divine favor, material provision, and protection—collectively manifest a clear intention that the Hebrew people flourish and experience well-being.
